safety_line: Skin secretions can irritate eyes, nose, and airways, especially for people with asthma, and can bother pets that mouth one. Wash hands after contact; see a doctor if irritation doesn’t clear up.

review.notes: Resolved 2026-09-26: EDIS UW259 ("The Cuban Treefrog in Florida") and UW394 ("Managing Conflicts with Wildlife: Living with Frogs") both loaded directly and confirm skin-secretion eye/nose/mucous-membrane irritation, pet mouth irritation, asthmatic/allergic reactions, and predation on native treefrogs (esp. squirrel treefrogs). safety_line and copy left as written; both URLs added to sources.

traits: Large warty treefrog, up to about 5 inches — the largest treefrog in the US
Oversized toe pads compared to native treefrogs
Common around porch lights at night hunting insects
Grayish, brownish, or greenish with variable blotching, and rough, warty skin

look_alikes.difference: Cuban treefrogs are much larger with warty skin and oversized toe pads; green treefrogs are smaller, smooth-skinned, and usually have a white side stripe.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the toe pads and overall size next to a coin.

look_alikes.difference: Cuban treefrog is much larger (to 5.5 in) with bumpy skin and huge bulging eyes; squirrel treefrog stays under 1.5 in with smooth skin and small eyes.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the eyes (bulging vs. normal) and skin texture (bumpy vs. smooth), next to something for size.

copy.what_it_means: An invasive species that eats Florida's smaller native treefrogs — one reason a porch chorus may have gone quiet. Wash hands after contact, and turning porch lights off (or switching to amber) removes the insect buffet that draws them in.
copy.fact: An invasive that eats Florida’s smaller native treefrogs — one reason your porch chorus may have gone quiet.
copy.blurb: Wash hands after contact. Turning porch lights off (or amber) removes the insect buffet that draws them.

tech_notes: Confirm size + toe pad size vs. native treefrogs. Humane removal/exclusion; avoid bare-hand contact due to skin secretions.
